title: One invoicing app shared by every customer company, with the tenant filter written into each query by hand
provenance: Synthetic system authored for this corpus (issue #744). Not derived from, or sanitized from, any real system: there is nothing to leak by omission.
notes: Holdout case 2 of 2 for #744. The corpus's first case whose tenants are our own customers inside one app and one database, rather than another company across a zone. That is why the tenant boundary here is not a trust boundary at all: every tenant's data sits in one zone, and the separation lives in a filter each query adds by hand. So the case punishes an analyst that reads only crossings: the two worst findings, invoice enumeration on the payment page and a cross-tenant invoice load, cross no zone the model can show. The object-level and field-level authorization questions are the ASVS half: an invoice loaded by a counting number, an edit form saved field for field, and a role enforced by hiding buttons. Held out of tuning: no diagnosis reads it, so it confirms a fix measured on the other cases.
